title: Common accessibility anti-patterns
learningObjectives: Explain common accessibility anti-patterns and apply inclusive web accessibility practices.

understand.concept: Common accessibility anti-patterns include clickable divs without keyboard behaviour, missing form labels, placeholder-only instructions, removed focus outlines, images with meaningless alt text, colour-only status, incorrect heading order, and ARIA that conflicts with native semantics.
understand.whyItMatters: These patterns create barriers even when a page looks polished. A practical audit checks semantics, keyboard use, names and descriptions, contrast, media alternatives, and responsive behaviour.
understand.analogy: An anti-pattern is a shortcut that appears to work in one situation but creates a hidden barrier for another user.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; accessible names, language, and interaction behaviour must follow platform accessibility rules.

explain.narrative: The example uses a native button, a visible label, text in addition to an icon, and a visible focus indicator.

practise.guidedTask: Audit a sample page for at least five anti-patterns. Replace non-semantic controls, add labels, restore focus visibility, and provide text alternatives.
practise.independentTask: Perform an accessibility review of a small page. Test keyboard-only use, labels, language metadata, media alternatives, and assistive technology output where available.
hints: Keep ARIA states synchronized with real interface state.
Provide text alternatives for meaningful non-text content.
